stem: Which type of Lightning page is used for one object, such as the Account page?

options.text: Record page
Home page
App page
Utility page

explanation: A record page is built for one object. App pages are standalone pages and home pages are the starting page.

stem: A new Lightning record page has been built but users still see the old layout. What is the likely cause?

options.text: The page has not been activated
The page layout is deleted
The profile has no licence
The field is hidden

explanation: A Lightning page only takes effect once it is activated as the org default, app default, or by app, record type and profile.

stem: Which TWO options can you use to activate a Lightning record page? (Choose 2)

options.text: Org default
App, record type and profile assignment
Role hierarchy
Sharing rule

explanation: You can activate a record page as the org default, an app default, or for a combination of app, record type and profile.

stem: A service team needs to work on many cases at once with tabs and subtabs. Which navigation style fits?

options.text: Console navigation
Standard navigation
Mobile navigation
Setup navigation

explanation: Console navigation uses tabs and subtabs so agents can handle multiple records without losing their place.

stem: What is a utility bar?

options.text: A docked toolbar at the bottom of an app for quick tools
A list of Setup pages that admins use most often
A type of report that shows items by owner
A dashboard filter that applies to every component

explanation: The utility bar holds tools such as notes, phone and recent items at the bottom of the app window.

stem: How are Lightning apps made available to users?

options.text: By assigning them to profiles
By sharing them with roles
By adding them to page layouts
By activating them in a report

explanation: Apps are assigned to profiles. Users see assigned apps in the app launcher.

objective: Use Dynamic Forms and component visibility
stem: What does Dynamic Forms let you do?

options.text: Place fields and sections on the Lightning page and give each a visibility rule
Create new custom fields automatically whenever a user types a new value
Replace profiles and permission sets with visibility rules on each field
Set field-level security separately for each section of the Lightning page and each user

explanation: Dynamic Forms move fields onto the Lightning page so you can show or hide them with rules, reducing the need for many layouts.

objective: Use Dynamic Forms and component visibility
stem: A section should appear only when Customer Type is Commercial. Which feature fits?

options.text: Component or field-section visibility filter
A validation rule that hides the section on save
A duplicate rule that checks the customer type
A sharing rule that limits the section to a group

explanation: Visibility filters show or hide a component or section based on a condition such as a field value.

objective: Explain page layouts and compact layouts
stem: What does a page layout control?

options.text: Fields, sections, related lists and buttons on a record
Which records a user can see in a list view
The login times that apply to a user
Which report folders a user can open

explanation: A page layout arranges the record page. It does not control data access.

objective: Explain page layouts and compact layouts
stem: What does a compact layout control?

options.text: The key fields in the highlights panel and in mobile
The columns shown in a report on the object
The fields shown in a list view on the object
The related lists shown on the record page

explanation: A compact layout chooses the important fields shown at the top of a record and in mobile.

objective: Explain page layouts and compact layouts
stem: How is a page layout assigned to users?

options.text: By profile and record type
By role, so each level of the hierarchy has its own layout
By permission set, which can hold a layout for each object
By public group, so that all members share one layout

explanation: The layout assignment grid sets which layout each profile and record type combination sees.

objective: Explain page layouts and compact layouts
stem: What do search layouts control?

options.text: The columns shown in search results and lookups
Who is allowed to search for records of the object
Which fields are searched when a user types a term
What appears on the home page after the search

explanation: Search layouts choose the columns shown in search results, lookup dialogs and list views of an object.

stem: Which is available at the top of any screen, such as the plus icon, to create a task from anywhere?

options.text: A global action
An object-specific action
A related list
A compact layout

explanation: Global actions are not tied to an object and appear in the global create menu.

stem: Which quick action type lets a user fire off a flow from a button on a record?

options.text: Flow action
Update a record action
Log a call action
Send email action

explanation: A quick action can launch a screen flow from a record page.

stem: What does Path provide?

options.text: A stage bar with key fields and guidance for each stage
A sharing rule that opens records to a stage owner
An email template that is sent when the stage changes
A report type that shows the records in each stage

explanation: Path shows the stages of a process and prompts for key fields and tips at each stage.

stem: What can an admin configure for each stage in a Path?

options.text: Key fields to prompt for and guidance for success
A sharing rule that decides who can see each stage
A validation rule that stops the stage from changing
A report filter that shows records in the stage

explanation: For each stage you choose key fields and write guidance for success, which appear when the user clicks the stage.

stem: A sales rep wants a saved, filtered table of her open deals to work through quickly. Which tool fits?

options.text: A list view
A matrix report
A dashboard
A page layout

explanation: A list view is a filtered table of records for working through them, with inline editing.

stem: Who can see a list view you create?

options.text: You choose: only you, all users, or selected groups and roles
Always everyone in the org, because list views cannot be restricted
Only admins, because list views are a Setup feature
Only the owner's manager and the people who report to the owner

explanation: List view visibility can be limited to the creator, set to all users, or shared with selected groups.

stem: Reps say the Opportunity page is cluttered with fields they never use. What is the best approach?

options.text: Use a focused Lightning record page with Dynamic Forms and hide what is irrelevant
Add more tabs so that reps can switch between groups of fields
Delete the unused fields from the object for every user
Give the reps a different licence with a smaller layout

explanation: Remove and group fields, and use visibility rules, rather than deleting data or adding tabs.

objective: Explain page layouts and compact layouts
stem: Hiding a field from a page layout does what?

options.text: Hides it on that layout only, but the data can still be exposed elsewhere
Makes the field secure everywhere, including reports and the API
Deletes the field and all of its data from the object
Hides it from reports and the API as well as from the layout

explanation: Layouts are about display. Field-level security is the control that truly hides a field.

stem: Which page type is a standalone page that you add to an app navigation?

options.text: App page
Record page
Email template
Report page

explanation: An app page is a standalone Lightning page not tied to a single object.

stem: Sales and Service teams want different home pages. Which feature controls this?

options.text: Lightning page assignment by app, record type or profile
A record type on Account assigned to the sales profile
A validation rule that checks which app is open
A report folder shared with each team

explanation: In Lightning App Builder you can activate pages for specific apps, record types and profiles.
